clues.text: A Moabite widow told her mother-in-law, "Your people will be my people, and your God will be my God."
Gleaning grain behind the harvesters near Bethlehem, she happened to come to the part of the field owned by Boaz.
On Naomi's advice, she went secretly to the threshing floor at night, uncovered a man's feet, and lay down.
Matthew's list of Jesus' ancestors names her as the mother of Obed, grandfather of King David.
The women of Bethlehem told Naomi this daughter-in-law loved her and was better to her than seven sons.
Before dawn, Boaz poured six measures of barley into her shawl so she would not return empty-handed.
At the town gate, before ten elders, Boaz bought Elimelech's land and took Mahlon's widow as his wife.
